bottom_line: In 804 men with chronic congestive heart failure receiving digoxin and diuretics, enalapril reduced two-year mortality to 18 percent vs 25 percent with hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate (P = 0.016).
implications: The trial supports that, in this population and dosing, two-year mortality was lower with enalapril (18 percent) than with hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate (25 percent; P = 0.016), with the difference attributed to fewer sudden deaths, while overall mortality over the full follow-up was not statistically significant (P = 0.08). It does not support concluding that enalapril improves peak oxygen consumption versus hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate, since oxygen consumption increased significantly only with hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate early in follow-up, and it does not show a between-group difference in pump-failure mortality.

major_points.text: Double-blind randomized comparison of enalapril vs hydralazine plus isosorbide dinitrate in 804 men on digoxin and diuretics.
major_points.quote:
we compared the effects of hydralazine and isosorbide dinitrate with those of enala-
pril in 804 men receiving digoxin and diuretic therapy for
heart failure. The patients were randomly assigned in a
double-blind manner

major_points.text: Intervention dosing was enalapril 20 mg daily vs hydralazine 300 mg plus isosorbide dinitrate 160 mg daily.
major_points.quote:
receive 20 mg of enalapril daily or
300 mg of hydralazine plus 160 mg of isosorbide dinitrate
daily.

major_points.text: Two-year mortality was significantly lower with enalapril than with hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate.
Overall mortality during follow-up was not statistically significant between groups.
major_points.quote:
This trend continued throughout the study but
did not quite attain statistical significance for the du-
ration of the follow-up period (P = 0.08).

major_points.text: Peak oxygen consumption increased with hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate early (13 weeks and 6 months) but not with enalapril.
major_points.quote:
Oxygen consumption was
increased significantly by hydralazine—isosorbide di-
nitrate after 13 weeks (by 0.6 ml per kilogram per
minute; P<0.0001) and after 6 months (by 0.8 ml per
kilogram per minute; P<0.0001), but not by enalapril.

major_points.text: Ejection fraction increased in both arms; the 13-week increase was greater with hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate.
major_points.quote:
The increase after 13 weeks in the
hydralazine—isosorbide dinitrate arm (0.033) was sig-
nificantly greater (P = 0.026) than the increase in the
enalapril arm (0.021).

inclusion_criteria.text: Men between the ages of 18 and 75 with chronic heart failure were recruited.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
Men between the ages of 18 and 75 with chronic heart failure
were recruited at 13 participating Veterans Affairs medical centers.

inclusion_criteria.text: Eligibility required evidence of cardiac dysfunction by cardiothoracic ratio, LV internal diameter, or ejection fraction.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
eligibility for the trial was determined on the
basis of evidence of cardiac dysfunction (cardiothoracic ratio =0.55
on chest radiography, left ventricular internal diameter >2.7 cm per
square meter of body-surface area at diastole on echocardiography,
or ejection fraction less than 0.45

inclusion_criteria.text: Required reduced exercise tolerance: dyspnea or fatigue at peak oxygen consumption <25 ml/kg/min.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
Reduced exercise tolerance was defined
as present when a test was terminated by dyspnea or fatigue occur-
ring at a peak oxygen consumption of less than 25 ml per kilogram
of body weight per minute.

inclusion_criteria.text: A baseline period of at least four weeks was required to establish optimal therapy with digoxin and a diuretic agent.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
a base-line period of at least four
weeks was required to establish optimal therapy with digoxin and a
diuretic agent

inclusion_criteria.text: Two consecutive exercise tests at least two weeks apart demonstrating respiratory stability and stable clinical state were required before randomization.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
Two consecutive exercise tests at least two weeks apart that showed
respiratory stability (peak oxygen consumption, <25 ml per kilo-
gram per minute, with a difference between tests of <4 ml per
kilogram per minute) and a stable clinical state

exclusion_criteria.text: Myocardial infarction or cardiac surgery within the previous three months.
exclusion_criteria.quote:
Reasons for exclusion from the study
included myocardial infarction or cardiac surgery within the previ-
ous three months

criticisms.text: No placebo group was included in the present study.
criticisms.quote:
No placebo group
was included in the present study

criticisms.text: Trial rationale notes it would be imprudent to leave a subgroup untreated with vasodilators for a long period (explaining lack of placebo arm).
criticisms.quote:
No placebo arm was included in the second trial, be-
cause after reviewing the findings of the earlier trial,
the investigators thought it would be imprudent to
leave a subgroup of patients untreated with vasodi-
lators for a long period.

criticisms.text: Patients with active ischemic heart disease were largely excluded due to exclusion of angina limiting exercise.
criticisms.quote:
Since angina limiting exercise
during the bicycle ergometer test before randomi-
zation was a criterion for exclusion, patients with
active ischemic heart disease were largely excluded.
